//self_name: This bridge's name: the admin's mailbox and what peers register it as. Empty means the hostname.
//description: One line on what this bridge is for. Peers see it in the MCP instructions.
//token: The ADMIN credential: may send as any name and read any mailbox. For the operator - scripts and local curl - not for an agent. Generated by 'agent-bridge init'.
//agents: One credential per agent ROLE - 'the Claude in repo-a', 'the Codex in repo-a', 'the bot on the other box' - wherever it runs. Generated by 'agent-bridge agent add <name> --description ...'. The name is the agent's identity: its messages carry it and it is the only mailbox that token can read. Never give an agent the admin token.
//allowed_hosts: Host headers the MCP transport will accept. Leave empty to derive this machine's names and IPs automatically. The SDK's own default is an EMPTY allowlist, which rejects everything but localhost with 421 Misdirected Request.
//roots: name -> absolute path of a source tree this bridge may read. Files are addressed as 'name:relative/path'.
//ripgrep_path: Optional path to rg when ripgrep is not on PATH. Empty looks on PATH; absent, bridge_grep falls back to a slower Python scan.
//mailbox_max_bytes: Retention: oldest READ messages are evicted past this many bytes of text, or past inbox_max messages. A single message may be at most max_message_bytes.
//mailbox_store: Where messages are persisted. Relative paths sit next to config.json. Set to "" to keep the mailbox in memory only, which loses unread mail on every restart.
//logs: Log FILENAMES served by logs_list/logs_read, found under any root even where bridge_read refuses to go (bin/, dist/). exe_names date a log against the executable beside it. Empty names means no log tools at all.

exec.//commands: Keyed by NAME; a caller never composes a command line. Each child gets a minimal environment (PATH, HOME, TEMP, the system vars) - never the server's own, which is where API keys live. A command that needs more sets it in its own "env" map. "root": "*" means the caller picks any root as the working directory.
